text:
leah: Hi all, I'm Leah, started this week. Trying to bootstrap dev on a company MacBook Pro (macOS 13). Quick list: homebrew/asdf, pyenv + poetry, SSH keys, and access to REDWOOD_API_KEY in 1Password. Hit two problems: Homebrew failed with permission errors, and asdf plugin-install for python times out on `gh` API rate limit.

omar: welcome! For Homebrew permissions, run: `/bin/bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Homebrew/install/HEAD/install.sh)"` then follow the post-install PATH steps. On macOS with M1/M2, make sure `/opt/homebrew` is owned by your user: `sudo chown -R $(whoami) /opt/homebrew`.

leah: I get `Error: Could not create /opt/homebrew/Cellar` when running brew.

it-bot: Device enrolled. MDM: Jamf; Security: Defender for Endpoint. Outbound connections proxied through corp proxy at 10.1.2.3:8080. Rate limits for GitHub API traced for this device. If you need GH tokens, request via dev-tools.

nina: for asdf/github rate limits, set a GH token env var before plugin install: `export GITHUB_TOKEN=ghp_xxx` (store token in 1Password and fetch with `op item get dev/github-token --fields label=token`). Then `asdf plugin-add python` should work. Also `asdf plugin-update --all` helps.

chris: for SSH, generate an ed25519 key in macOS and add to your GitHub account. Commands: `ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C "leah@redwood.ai"` then `pbcopy < ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub` and paste into GH. If you use 1Password SSH agent, add the key there so it syncs across devices.

leah: how do I install pyenv via asdf? I usually use pyenv standalone.

omar: with asdf: `asdf plugin-add python && asdf install python 3.11.6 && asdf global python 3.11.6`. For poetry, `pipx install poetry` or `curl -sSL https://install.python-poetry.org | python3 -` then `poetry config virtualenvs.in-project true`. We prefer in-project venvs for reproducibility.

leah: brew still errors until I fix ownership, but when I `chown` it asks for sudo and then brew doctor shows missing deps. Any recommended minimal formulae to install?

nina: install git, openssl, gnupg, node, docker: `brew install git openssl gnupg node docker docker-compose`. For local containers we expect Docker Desktop, but many devs use Colima on macs: `brew install colima` and `colima start --cpu 4 --memory 8` if Docker Desktop is refused by IT.

leah: Colima looks promising. Does dev flow require Docker Desktop specifically?

chris: most devcontainers work with Colima + Docker CLI, but VSCode's Docker extension integrates better with Docker Desktop. For our dev workflow, Colima is supported but you may need to tweak docker-compose files for macos volumes. If you run into issues, ping `#eng` with logs.

leah: last thing: how do I fetch REDWOOD_API_KEY into my local env securely? I don't want to paste in plaintext.

it-bot: Use 1Password CLI or the internal CLI. Device policy allows `op` on this device.

omar: recommended: install `op`, then run `eval $(op signin redwood)` and `export REDWOOD_API_KEY=$(op item get dev/redwood/api-key --fields label=key)`. Alternatively, add a line to your `~/.env.local` and .gitignore that file. We discourage committing secrets.

nina: small tip: add `.envrc` to repo and use direnv `brew install direnv` then `direnv allow` to auto-load env vars from `.envrc` (local-only). Great for reducing copy/paste.

leah: thanks everyone! If no blockers after I finish chowning brew, can someone from infra approve GH token request? @omar can you help?

omar: sure, I will create a request with dev-tools and tag infra. Also happy to pair later today if needed.

leah: appreciate it :heart:
